title: PR #3710: provide beads-only repro for 12s slow path (perf/dolt) per @coffeegoddd review
description:
Address @coffeegoddd's review on gastownhall/beads PR #3710 (perf(dolt): eliminate 12s slow path on bd commands when .local_version is stale).

## Finding to address
@coffeegoddd: 'We need a beads-only repro of this to prove it's a bug. What is the version of the go/bin/beads, and the version of the .local/usr/bin/beads, and what bd commands do we run with which version to see the 12s latency?'

In short: the PR lacks a minimal reproducible example that proves the latency issue exists and that this change fixes it.

## What to do
1. Read the PR diff and existing description to understand the 12s slow path claim
2. Construct a beads-only repro:
   - Document exact versions of go/bin/beads vs .local/usr/bin/beads where the 12s latency appears
   - List the exact bd commands to run to observe the latency
   - Show the fix eliminates it (before/after timing)
3. Add this repro to the PR description or as a PR comment responding to @coffeegoddd
4. If code changes are also needed to better document or test the fix, include them

## After
Respond to @coffeegoddd on the PR with the repro information. Appreciate the feedback.

## Acceptance criteria
- Repro steps documented: versions, commands, observed timing (before: ~12s, after: fast)
- PR comment posted responding to @coffeegoddd's request
- If code changes: CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./... passes
close_reason: Repro script and REPRO.md committed (be-vxngmn), PR comment responding to coffeegoddd already posted. All acceptance criteria met.

title: PR #4055: fix doubled 'Error: Error:' in rejectProtectedConfigKey via FatalError (be-udvd)
description:
Address @maphew's review on gastownhall/beads PR #4055 (refactor(errors): replace fmt.Fprintf+os.Exit with FatalError*).

## Finding to address
cmd/bd/config.go:97 now does FatalError("%s", msg) for rejectProtectedConfigKey.
But rejectProtectedConfigKey (config.go:780) already returns a message starting with 'Error:'.
FatalError adds another 'Error:' prefix -> user sees 'Error: Error: issue_prefix cannot be set...'

Reproducer:
  CGO_ENABLED=0 go run ./cmd/bd config set issue_prefix foo
  # prints: Error: Error: issue_prefix cannot be set via 'bd config set'.

Also affects --json output (legacy 'Error:' text appears inside the structured error field).

## Fix options (pick one)
A) Strip the leading 'Error: ' from rejectProtectedConfigKey's return message so FatalError adds it once
B) Keep that specific path as direct stderr output (since it is intentionally preformatted)

Either approach is fine — pick whichever is cleaner given the rest of the refactor.

## After code fix
Respond to @maphew appreciatively on the PR. This is a legitimate review response — not a ping.

## Acceptance criteria
- CGO_ENABLED=0 go run ./cmd/bd config set issue_prefix foo outputs EXACTLY one 'Error:' prefix
- CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./cmd/bd -run TestRejectProtectedConfigKey passes and CATCHES the doubled prefix (update test if it only checks substring)
- PR comment posted responding to @maphew's finding
close_reason: Test added to assert no 'Error:' prefix in rejectProtectedConfigKey message; pushed cc5ed38ec; maphew thanked on PR.

title: PR #4153: fix git+https/git+ssh/SCP URL normalization in dolt collision guard + bd doctor (be-7eu1d)
description:
Address @maphew's 2026-06-14 review on gastownhall/beads PR #4153 (feat(dolt): git-origin collision guard).

## Findings to address

### 1. Collision guard misses Dolt-normalized remote URL forms
cmd/bd/dolt_remote_guard.go only strips .git and trailing slashes. Must also handle:
- git+https://github.com/org/repo.git
- git+ssh://...
- SCP-style: git@github.com:org/repo.git

These are first-class Dolt remote URL forms. Create a shared Dolt-aware URL comparator.

### 2. bd doctor has same normalization gap
cmd/bd/doctor/remotes.go compares SQL remotes to git origin through its own simple helper.
Should use the SAME shared Dolt-aware comparator so both paths stay in sync.

### 3. Test tag mismatch
Test file is tagged embeddeddolt but calls helpers from cgo-tagged test files.
`go test -tags 'embeddeddolt gms_pure_go' ./cmd/bd` fails to compile.
Resolve the build-tag dependency so coverage is reliable under declared tags.

## Stacking note
@maphew also noted this PR is stacked on #4151 (still open). Evaluate: can we fix the 3 findings above on just this PR's changes independently, or does #4151 need to land first? If stacking is required, note that in the PR response.

## After code fix
Respond to @maphew appreciatively on the PR, noting each finding was addressed. This is a legitimate review response on our own PR — not a ping.

## Acceptance criteria
- normalizeRemoteURL() (or equivalent shared helper) handles git+https://, git+ssh://, SCP-style
- bd doctor remotes path uses same shared helper
- CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -tags gms_pure_go ./cmd/bd/doctor passes
- go test -tags 'embeddeddolt gms_pure_go' ./cmd/bd compiles clean
- PR comment posted responding to @maphew's findings
close_reason: All 3 maphew findings addressed: doltremote.CanonicalForComparison() shared helper, doctor remotes updated, build tag fixed to embeddeddolt && cgo. Pushed 67bb5fba2, maphew thanked on PR.

title: Architecture: routed embedded writes need a writable target open without re-breaking .32/GH#3231 read-only hydration (beads main RED)
description:
# Architecture: Routed Embedded Writes — `OpenWritable` Mode + Resolver Split

**Bead:** be-4hzi  
**Priority:** P1 — beads main RED  
**Date:** 2026-06-10  
**Regressor:** bd-6dnrw.32 (`store_factory.go:182` `Open` → `OpenReadOnly`)

---

## Requirements

### Functional
- **FR-1:** Routed write commands (`update`, `comment`, `note`, `reopen`, `assign`, `priority`, `tag`, `delete`, `dep`, `edit`, …) MUST commit to the target store when the issue is resolved via prefix routing.
- **FR-2:** Routed writes via auto-routing fallback MUST also commit to the target.
- **FR-3:** Cross-repo hydration reads (show, list, completions, importers) MUST continue to open foreign databases without running the migration gate, applying migrations, or writing anything into the target's history.
- **FR-4:** `TestEmbeddedOpenReadOnly_SkipsGateAndMigrations` MUST stay green — `OpenReadOnly` is unchanged.
- **FR-5:** `TestEmbeddedUpdateRoutedStoreCommitsTargetHead` and `TestEmbeddedRoutedSiblingWritesCommitTargetHead` MUST pass.

### Non-Functional
- **NFR-1:** The fix MUST NOT re-open GH#3231/#4259: no auto-migration of foreign projects, no schema fork risk.
- **NFR-2:** The fix MUST NOT revert bd-6dnrw.32.
- **NFR-3:** Data-integrity guarantee: writing to a schema-behind target MUST fail fast with a clear error rather than with a cryptic SQL failure.
- **NFR-4:** Contributor boundary: no upstream PRs modified, no upstream branches touched.

---

## Constraints

| Type       | Constraint                                                                                            |
|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Technical  | Must preserve `OpenReadOnly` behavior; test `TestEmbeddedOpenReadOnly_SkipsGateAndMigrations` is contractual. |
| Technical  | Must not run `MigrateUp` on a foreign target (GH#3231/#4259 — schema fork on remote-backed DB).       |
| Technical  | Must not run the remote-migrate gate on the routed target (gate hard-fails on behind/remote-backed DBs). |
| Business   | beads main is RED; fix must be minimal, surgical, and reviewable by upstream maintainers.              |
| Regulatory | We are contributors, not maintainers. We cannot merge or modify upstream PRs.                         |

---

## Root Cause Analysis

`newReadOnlyStoreFromConfig` is the shared open-path for ALL routing:

```
resolveViaPrefixRouting  ─► newReadOnlyStoreFromConfig ─► OpenReadOnly (write-blocked)
resolveViaAutoRouting    ─► openRoutedReadStore         ─► newReadOnlyStoreFromConfig ─► OpenReadOnly (write-blocked)
```

Before bd-6dnrw.32, both paths called `embeddeddolt.Open` (writable). .32 changed
`newReadOnlyStoreFromConfig` to call `embeddeddolt.OpenReadOnly`, which correctly protects
hydration reads but incorrectly blocks ALL routed writes (`withConn(commit=true)` returns
`errReadOnly`).

The routing resolver is a **single function** (`resolveAndGetIssueWithRouting`) serving both
reads and writes. It returns a `RoutedResult.Store` that the caller then uses for its
operation — but the store's read/write mode was fixed at open time, before the caller's
intent was known.

---

## Decision: Option B — `OpenWritable` mode + writable resolver factories

**Rejected: Option A** (revert `newReadOnlyStoreFromConfig` to `Open`) — re-opens the
remote-migrate gate on the hydration read path, re-breaking GH#3231/#4259.  
**Rejected: Option C** (revert .32) — re-breaks `TestEmbeddedOpenReadOnly_SkipsGateAndMigrations`.

---

## Open Mode Comparison

| Property                | `Open` (local primary) | `OpenReadOnly` (.32) | `OpenWritable` (new) |
|-------------------------|------------------------|----------------------|----------------------|
| CREATE DATABASE         | ✓                      | ✗                    | ✗                    |
| Remote-migrate gate     | ✓                      | ✗                    | ✗                    |
| MigrateUp               | ✓                      | ✗                    | ✗                    |
| CheckForwardDrift       | ✗ (MigrateUp covers it)| ✓                    | ✓                    |
| Backward-drift check    | ✗                      | ✗ (read-safe)        | ✓ (write-safety)     |
| Write transactions      | ✓                      | ✗                    | ✓                    |
| Use case                | Local primary store    | Foreign hydration reads | Routed writes to foreign store |

---

## Layer 1 — New `embeddeddolt.OpenWritable` API

**Location:** `internal/storage/embeddeddolt/store.go`

```go
// OpenWritable opens an existing embedded database for writable access with no
// auto-migration side-effects. Like OpenReadOnly, it skips CREATE DATABASE, the
// remote-migrate gate, and MigrateUp — so it does not fork the schema of a
// remote-backed foreign project (GH#3231/#4259). Unlike OpenReadOnly, write
// transactions are allowed so that routed writes (update, comment, note, etc.)
// can commit to the target.
//
// Forward drift (DB ahead of binary) is checked: a stale-binary write to a
// schema-ahead target would produce invalid data. Backward drift (target schema
// behind binary) is also checked: writing from a binary that knows about columns
// the target doesn't have yet risks data corruption.
//
// Use for routed writes to a foreign project. Use OpenReadOnly for hydration reads.
func OpenWritable(ctx context.Context, beadsDir, database, branch string) (*EmbeddedDoltStore, error) {
    // ... validate inputs and resolve absBeadsDir ...
    // ... verify dataDir exists (no MkdirAll — target must already be initialized) ...

    s := &EmbeddedDoltStore{
        dataDir:  dataDir,
        beadsDir: absBeadsDir,
        database: database,
        branch:   branch,
        readOnly: false,  // ← write transactions allowed
    }

    db, cleanup, err := OpenSQL(ctx, dataDir, database, branch)
    // ...
    defer func() { _ = cleanup() }()

    // Forward drift: DB is ahead of binary → reads and writes would be invalid.
    if err := schema.CheckForwardDrift(ctx, db); err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }

    // Backward drift: binary is ahead of DB → writes may reference columns/tables
    // that don't exist yet in the target. Reject explicitly rather than letting SQL
    // fail cryptically.
    if err := checkBackwardDrift(ctx, db); err != nil {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("embeddeddolt: cannot open routed target for writing: %w", err)
    }

    return s, nil
}
```

### Backward drift check

```go
// checkBackwardDrift returns an error if the database schema version is behind
// the binary's expected version. This guards routed writes: writing from a binary
// that expects a newer schema than the target has risks data corruption.
func checkBackwardDrift(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB) error {
    var currentVersion int
    if err := db.QueryRowContext(ctx,
        "SELECT COALESCE(MAX(version), 0) FROM schema_migrations",
    ).Scan(&currentVersion); err != nil {
        return nil // schema_migrations doesn't exist → fresh DB, not an issue
    }
    if currentVersion < schema.LatestVersion() {
        return &RoutedSchemaBehindError{
            DBVersion:     currentVersion,
            BinaryVersion: schema.LatestVersion(),
        }
    }
    return nil
}
```

`RoutedSchemaBehindError` message (user-facing):
> "routed target schema is at v%d, this binary expects v%d — run 'bd doctor' or 'bd upgrade' on the target repository to apply pending migrations, then retry"

**Note:** If `schema_migrations` is absent (fresh DB, version 0), backward drift is a
false positive — the target hasn't been initialized yet. Treat version 0 as "schema not
yet present" and skip the check (same as `checkSchemaSkew` behavior for fresh DBs).
Concrete rule: skip backward drift check when `currentVersion == 0`.

---

## Layer 2 — New `newWritableNoMigrateStoreFromConfig` factory

**Location:** `cmd/bd/store_factory.go` (cgo) and `cmd/bd/store_factory_nocgo.go` (no-cgo)

### cgo (`store_factory.go`)

```go
// newWritableNoMigrateStoreFromConfig opens the store at beadsDir for writing
// without running CREATE DATABASE, the remote-migrate gate, or MigrateUp.
// Used for routed writes to foreign projects (GH#3231/#4259).
func newWritableNoMigrateStoreFromConfig(ctx context.Context, beadsDir string) (storage.DoltStorage, error) {
    cfg, err := configfile.Load(beadsDir)
    if err == nil && cfg != nil && cfg.IsDoltProxiedServerMode() {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("proxy server store should be uow provider")
    }
    if err == nil && cfg != nil && cfg.IsDoltServerMode() {
        // Server mode: dolt sql-server handles migration lifecycle; no embedded gate needed.
        return dolt.NewFromConfig(ctx, beadsDir)
    }
    database := configfile.DefaultDoltDatabase
    if cfg != nil {
        database = cfg.GetDoltDatabase()
    }
    if sanitized := sanitizeDBName(database); sanitized != database {
        database = sanitized // in-memory sanitize only; do not rename or persist
    }
    return embeddeddolt.OpenWritable(ctx, beadsDir, database, "main")
}
```

**Server-mode note:** `dolt.NewFromConfig` is the same as `newDoltStoreFromConfig` for
the server path — server mode routes SQL over a network connection, has no local embedded
migration machinery, and the `ReadOnly: true` flag in `newReadOnlyStoreFromConfig` was
suppressing writes at the connection level. For routed writes, use the default writable
connection.

### no-cgo (`store_factory_nocgo.go`)

```go
func newWritableNoMigrateStoreFromConfig(ctx context.Context, beadsDir string) (storage.DoltStorage, error) {
    cfg, err := configfile.Load(beadsDir)
    if err == nil && cfg != nil && cfg.IsDoltProxiedServerMode() {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("proxy server store should be uow provider")
    }
    if err == nil && cfg != nil && cfg.IsDoltServerMode() {
        return dolt.NewFromConfig(ctx, beadsDir)
    }
    return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s", nocgoEmbeddedErrMsg)
}
```

---

## Layer 3 — Resolver change: `resolveViaPrefixRouting`

**Location:** `cmd/bd/routed.go:191`

Change:
```go
targetStore, err := newReadOnlyStoreFromConfig(ctx, targetBeadsDir)
```
to:
```go
targetStore, err := newWritableNoMigrateStoreFromConfig(ctx, targetBeadsDir)
```

This is the primary fix for the failing tests. Prefix-routed stores are now
writable-no-migrate. Read commands that happen to go through prefix routing are
unaffected — a writable-no-migrate store is a superset of a read-only store.

---

## Layer 4 — Resolver change: `openRoutedReadStore` → `openRoutedStore`

**Location:** `cmd/bd/routing_read.go:104`

Change:
```go
targetStore, err := newReadOnlyStoreFromConfig(ctx, targetBeadsDir)
```
to:
```go
targetStore, err := newWritableNoMigrateStoreFromConfig(ctx, targetBeadsDir)
```

**Rename** the function from `openRoutedReadStore` to `openRoutedStore` to reflect that
the returned store is general-purpose (writable-no-migrate), not read-only. Update all
call sites (`close.go`, `list.go`, `ready.go`, `routed.go`). This also fixes the
previously-invisible breakage of auto-routing write fallbacks in `resolveViaAutoRouting`.

---

## Data Model (unchanged)

No schema changes. The fix is entirely in open-mode semantics and the routing open-path.

```mermaid
erDiagram
    EmbeddedDoltStore {
        string dataDir
        string beadsDir
        string database
        string branch
        bool readOnly
    }
```

---

## Use Cases

### UC-1: Routed prefix write (fixed)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["bd update tgt-8wn --title 'Fixed'"] --> B[resolveAndGetIssueWithRouting]
    B --> C{Local store has tgt-8wn?}
    C -- No --> D[resolveViaPrefixRouting]
    D --> E[newWritableNoMigrateStoreFromConfig]
    E --> F[OpenWritable\nskip gate, skip MigrateUp\nallow writes]
    F --> G[RoutedResult.Store = writable]
    G --> H[UpdateIssue → withConn commit=true]
    H --> I[DOLT_COMMIT on target HEAD]
    I --> J["✓ target HEAD advanced"]
```

### UC-2: Cross-repo hydration read (unchanged)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["bd show tgt-8wn"] --> B[resolveAndGetIssueWithRouting]
    B --> C{Local store has tgt-8wn?}
    C -- No --> D[resolveViaPrefixRouting]
    D --> E[newWritableNoMigrateStoreFromConfig]
    E --> F[OpenWritable\nskip gate, skip MigrateUp\nallow writes — but caller never writes]
    F --> G[RoutedResult.Store]
    G --> H[GetIssue → withConn commit=false]
    H --> I["✓ read completes, target unchanged"]
```

### UC-3: Hydration read via importer / openReadOnlyStoreForDBPath (unchanged)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["github/gitlab/linear importer"] --> B[openReadOnlyStoreForDBPath]
    B --> C[newReadOnlyStoreFromConfig]
    C --> D[OpenReadOnly\nskip gate, skip MigrateUp\nrefuse writes]
    D --> E["✓ target not mutated (GH#3231)"]
```

---

## Action Flows

### AF-1: OpenWritable open sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Caller (routing resolver)
    participant OW as OpenWritable
    participant SQL as OpenSQL
    participant FD as CheckForwardDrift
    participant BD as checkBackwardDrift

    C->>OW: OpenWritable(ctx, beadsDir, database, branch)
    OW->>OW: validate inputs, resolve absBeadsDir
    OW->>OW: stat dataDir (must exist — no MkdirAll)
    OW->>SQL: OpenSQL(ctx, dataDir, database, branch)
    SQL-->>OW: db, cleanup
    OW->>FD: CheckForwardDrift(ctx, db)
    alt DB ahead of binary
        FD-->>OW: SchemaSkewError
        OW-->>C: error (stale binary)
    end
    OW->>BD: checkBackwardDrift(ctx, db)
    alt Binary ahead of DB (schema behind, not version 0)
        BD-->>OW: RoutedSchemaBehindError
        OW-->>C: error (target needs upgrade)
    end
    OW->>OW: cleanup()
    OW-->>C: *EmbeddedDoltStore{readOnly: false}
```

1. Validate database name and resolve absolute path.
2. Stat the data directory — target must already exist; no auto-create (we are a foreign contributor).
3. Open a short-lived SQL connection to run the drift checks.
4. Run `CheckForwardDrift`: if the DB schema version exceeds the binary's expected version, the binary is stale and writes would be invalid → return `SchemaSkewError`.
5. Run `checkBackwardDrift`: if the DB schema version is below the binary's expected version AND is nonzero (not an uninitialized DB), the target needs migration → return `RoutedSchemaBehindError` with a clear upgrade hint.
6. Release the temporary SQL connection.
7. Return the `EmbeddedDoltStore` with `readOnly: false` — write transactions are now allowed.

---

## Security Controls

| Control              | Mechanism                                                             |
|----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Schema isolation     | No MigrateUp in `OpenWritable` — cannot fork a remote-backed schema  |
| Stale-binary guard   | `CheckForwardDrift` rejects writes from a binary behind the DB       |
| Behind-target guard  | `checkBackwardDrift` rejects writes to a DB behind the binary        |
| Gate bypass          | Remote-migrate gate intentionally skipped (foreign repo, not owner)  |
| Contributor boundary | No upstream PR modification; fix lives in contributor branch only    |

---

## Integrations

| Direction | Protocol | Auth            | SLA notes                                         |
|-----------|----------|-----------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| Routed writes → target store | embedded Dolt file I/O | process-local flock | Target must be on same machine |
| Prefix routing → routes.jsonl | file read | none | routes.jsonl must exist in source .beads/         |

---

## Risks

| Risk                                          | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation                                    |
|-----------------------------------------------|------------|--------|-----------------------------------------------|
| `OpenWritable` accidentally runs MigrateUp    | Low        | High   | Unit test verifies no schema_migrations writes |
| `OpenWritable` accidentally runs gate         | Low        | High   | Same test: gate-exempt open on behind/remote-backed DB |
| Backward-drift check too aggressive (false positives on version 0) | Medium | Low | Skip check when `currentVersion == 0` |
| Server-mode `dolt.NewFromConfig` opens with unexpected write permissions | Low | Medium | Server mode already used writable config for `newDoltStoreFromConfig`; no behavior change |
| Rename of `openRoutedReadStore` → `openRoutedStore` breaks callers | Low | Low | All callers are in `cmd/bd`; grep all references before committing |

---

## Trade-offs & Alternatives Considered

### Why not Option A (revert factory to `Open`)?
`newReadOnlyStoreFromConfig` is also called by hydration readers (importers, `openReadOnlyStoreForDBPath`). Calling `Open` there re-runs the remote-migrate gate and `MigrateUp` on every foreign project open — exactly the scenario GH#3231/#4259 guards against.

### Why not a per-caller intent flag on `resolveAndGetIssueWithRouting`?
The resolver is called by ~15 write commands and ~10 read commands. Threading a `writable bool` through every call site would require a 20+ site diff and make the resolver's signature unstable. The cleaner boundary is at the factory/open level: the routing factory always returns writable-no-migrate, which is a safe superset of read-only for all callers.

### Why is writable-no-migrate safe for read-only callers?
A writable-no-migrate store does not issue writes unless a caller explicitly calls a write method. Read commands (`bd show`, `bd list`, `bd ready`) never call write methods through the `RoutedResult.Store`. The `readOnly: false` flag only controls whether `withConn(commit=true)` is rejected — it doesn't issue spontaneous writes.

### Why reject backward drift rather than silently allow it?
Allowing writes to a schema-behind target risks one of:
- Silent success that writes data to existing columns while new columns get default/null values the user didn't intend
- Cryptic `column not found` SQL error that surfaces nothing actionable

A `RoutedSchemaBehindError` with an explicit "run bd doctor on the target" message is strictly better UX and prevents silent data skew.

### Why not migrate-then-write for a behind target?
This was the exact pattern that caused GH#3231/#4259 — when multiple clones independently auto-migrate, they fork the schema history on a remote-backed Dolt database. We cannot migrate foreign targets; we can only reject writes to behind targets.

---

## Files Affected

| File                                               | Change                                              |
|----------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| `internal/storage/embeddeddolt/store.go`           | Add `OpenWritable`, `checkBackwardDrift`, `RoutedSchemaBehindError` |
| `cmd/bd/store_factory.go`                          | Add `newWritableNoMigrateStoreFromConfig`           |
| `cmd/bd/store_factory_nocgo.go`                    | Add `newWritableNoMigrateStoreFromConfig`           |
| `cmd/bd/routed.go:191`                             | Change `newReadOnlyStoreFromConfig` → `newWritableNoMigrateStoreFromConfig` |
| `cmd/bd/routing_read.go:104`                       | Same change; rename `openRoutedReadStore` → `openRoutedStore` |
| `cmd/bd/close.go`, `list.go`, `ready.go`, `routed.go` | Update callers of `openRoutedReadStore` to new name |

---

## Tests

### Must stay green (do not touch)
- `internal/storage/embeddeddolt/remote_migrate_gate_test.go::TestEmbeddedOpenReadOnly_SkipsGateAndMigrations`

### Must pass after fix
- `cmd/bd/update_embedded_test.go::TestEmbeddedUpdateRoutedStoreCommitsTargetHead`
- `cmd/bd/autocommit_embedded_test.go::TestEmbeddedRoutedSiblingWritesCommitTargetHead`

### New tests for `OpenWritable` (add to `remote_migrate_gate_test.go` or a new file)
1. `TestEmbeddedOpenWritable_SkipsGateAndMigrations` — `OpenWritable` on a behind, remote-backed DB succeeds (same exemption as `OpenReadOnly`); no new commits/dirty tables
2. `TestEmbeddedOpenWritable_AllowsWriteTransactions` — `SetConfig` on an `OpenWritable` store succeeds (verify `readOnly: false` works end-to-end)
3. `TestEmbeddedOpenWritable_RejectsSchemaAheadDB` — `OpenWritable` on a DB one version ahead fails with `SchemaSkewError`
4. `TestEmbeddedOpenWritable_RejectsSchemaBehindNonZeroDB` — `OpenWritable` on a DB one version behind fails with `RoutedSchemaBehindError`
5. `TestEmbeddedOpenWritable_FreshDBSkipsBackwardDriftCheck` — `OpenWritable` on a fresh DB (version 0) succeeds (no false positive)

---

## Guardrails for Builder

1. **DO NOT** modify `OpenReadOnly`. Its test is contractual.
2. **DO NOT** run `MigrateUp` or the remote-migrate gate inside `OpenWritable` — this reopens GH#3231/#4259.
3. **DO NOT** add `readOnly: true` to any code path that uses `newWritableNoMigrateStoreFromConfig`.
4. `checkBackwardDrift` MUST skip the check when `currentVersion == 0` (fresh DB before `initSchema` has run).
5. When renaming `openRoutedReadStore` → `openRoutedStore`, grep all files under `cmd/bd/` before committing to catch any call site the grep above may have missed.
6. The backward-drift check in `OpenWritable` is NEW and does not exist in `OpenReadOnly`. Do NOT backport it to `OpenReadOnly` — read-only opens of behind targets should still work (needed for cross-rig show/list commands that pre-date a target upgrade).

---

## Handoff

Child beads (needs-design) will be created for the builder covering:
- `OpenWritable` implementation + tests
- Factory + resolver changes

title: beads main RED ~18h: embeddeddolt routed writes fail 'store is read-only' (regressor 3f2b4e08d / bd-6dnrw.32)
description:
## Symptom
`main` (gastownhall/beads) is RED on every push since ~2026-06-10 03:00 PT (~18h). The "Main" CI workflow fails on two embedded-dolt-cmd shards on EVERY main commit incl. current HEAD 001c6c258:
- Test (Embedded Dolt Cmd 8/20): FAIL TestEmbeddedUpdateRoutedStoreCommitsTargetHead
- Test (Embedded Dolt Cmd 12/20): FAIL TestEmbeddedRoutedSiblingWritesCommitTargetHead (comment/note/reopen subtests)

All fail with `embeddeddolt: store is read-only` when a routed write (bd update/comment/note/reopen targeting a sibling/target store) tries to commit the target head. Blocks clean CI on ALL beads PRs (they inherit it via rebase, e.g. PR #3663) and means no main commit is green.

## Bisection
- GREEN through 99c70904f ("Main" run success, 2026-06-10 02:53)
- RED from f1c72dbde onward ("Main" run failure 03:22, same two shards)
- Regressor batch 99c70904f..f1c72dbde = bd-6dnrw.29 .. .34 (6 commits)
- Note: #4141 (a0f9b880e, 2026-06-03) ADDED these tests and was GREEN at the time, so the tests are valid; a later commit regressed them.

## Root cause (identified by bisection + code-path trace + error-string match; NOT yet revert-confirmed)
Regressor: **3f2b4e08d** `fix(embeddeddolt): give read-only opens a real read-only path (bd-6dnrw.32)`.
It (1) introduced the read-only store mechanism in internal/storage/embeddeddolt/store.go (readOnly field, OpenReadOnly, errReadOnly; write/commit guards at store.go:167-168 and :211-212), and (2) changed cmd/bd/store_factory.go:186 so newReadOnlyStoreFromConfig (embedded path) calls embeddeddolt.OpenReadOnly (genuinely read-only) instead of embeddeddolt.Open (which returned a WRITABLE store despite the function name).

The routed-WRITE path opens its target store via that same factory and then writes to it:
- cmd/bd/routed.go:191  targetStore, err := newReadOnlyStoreFromConfig(ctx, targetBeadsDir)

Before 3f2b4e08d the target was writable, so routed writes committed the target head. After it the target is genuinely read-only -> routed write hits errReadOnly. The commit's intent (don't migrate/mutate foreign DBs during read-only cross-repo hydration, GH#3231) is correct; it broke routed-write callers that relied on the old writable-despite-the-name behavior.

## Suggested fix direction (DESIGN-SENSITIVE -- bd-6dnrw owner / architect)
Routed WRITES must get a WRITABLE target handle, not newReadOnlyStoreFromConfig. Options to weigh:
- a writable-but-no-migrate open (skip remote-migrate gate + migrations like OpenReadOnly, but permit writes), or
- a dedicated writable target factory for routed writes, keeping newReadOnlyStoreFromConfig read-only for hydration.
Audit all newReadOnlyStoreFromConfig callers for read-vs-write intent: cmd/bd/routed.go:191, cmd/bd/routing_read.go:104, cmd/bd/store_reopen.go:25/29. Do NOT blind-patch -- this touches the read-only-open contract bd-6dnrw.32 intentionally added.

- TestEmbeddedUpdateRoutedStoreCommitsTargetHead (cmd/bd/update_embedded_test.go)
- TestEmbeddedRoutedSiblingWritesCommitTargetHead (cmd/bd/autocommit_embedded_test.go)
Run via embedded-dolt cmd suite (BEADS_TEST_EMBEDDED_DOLT=1). Both must pass on main after the fix.

## Left for owner
Did NOT run revert-test of 3f2b4e08d^ vs 3f2b4e08d (heavy embedded-dolt build). Regressor identified by bisection + exact caller trace + error-string match. Owner should confirm by patching routed.go's target open and running the two tests.

## Provenance
Found by beads/investigator auditing PR #3663 CI (bead be-hstf). PR #3663 is blameless for these shards; its own required-gate failure (stale testing.Short allowlist) was fixed separately.

title: Root cause: 11 CI-failing beads PRs share one now-fixed main regression (routed read-only); rebase needed
description:
# Root cause (PROVEN): 11 CI-failing PRs share ONE now-fixed main regression

## Summary
The hourly `pr-audit` order filed 16 audit beads (double-filed as 32, see "Process
notes") routed to `beads/investigator`. Investigation shows the **11 "CI failing"
PRs all share a single root cause**, and the **5 "stale audit" PRs are a separate
matter** (0 failing checks — pure staleness).

All 11 CI-failing PRs fail **only** the `PR Risk` workflow, on
`Test (Embedded Dolt Cmd 8/20)` & `12/20`, with:

```
update_embedded_test.go:190: bd update <id> --title ... failed: exit status 1
    Error updating <id>: embeddeddolt: store is read-only
--- FAIL: TestEmbeddedUpdateRoutedStoreCommitsTargetHead
--- FAIL: TestEmbeddedRoutedSiblingWritesCommitTargetHead (comment/note/reopen)
```

The regular `PR` gate (`CI Gate / Required`) PASSES on all of them. These tests
exercise the **routed cross-store write** path and are unrelated to what any of
these PRs change (error-handling, perf, schema output, etc.).

## Root cause — a main-side regression, ALREADY FIXED on current main
- `PR Risk` builds the embedded `bd` binary with `-race` (`go build -tags gms_pure_go -race`)
  and runs it in embedded mode. The failure is **not** a data race (CI exits 1, not 66) —
  `-race` only changes timing, exposing a concurrency/timing path under full parallel
  shard load that leaves the routed-WRITE **target** store read-only.
- The commit guard at `internal/storage/embeddeddolt/store.go:180`
  (`if commit && s.readOnly { return errReadOnly }`) then refuses the routed update.
  The guard family was hardened by `8a92dacf4` (bd-578h9.12, Jun 11):
  "read-only stores refuse VC mutations".
- The routed-write path `cmd/bd/routed.go:218-221` (`resolveViaPrefixRoutingMode`,
  forWrite → `newDoltStoreFromConfig` → `embeddeddolt.Open`) is *supposed* to open the
  target writable; under concurrent shard load on the broken-window code it does not.

## Proof (bracket reproduction, local, CI-exact)
- Built `-race` binaries (`-tags gms_pure_go`), ran `embedded-test-shard.sh 8 20`:
  - **`8a92dacf4` (Jun 11): shard 8 FAILS** — exact `store is read-only` error reproduced.
  - **`e8ae7a29` (main HEAD, Jun 13): shard 8 PASSES 5/5; shard 12 (sibling) PASSES.**
- Single test in isolation PASSES even with `-race` — the failure requires the full
  parallel shard. `PR Risk` triggers on `pull_request`/`merge_group` only, **not main
  push**, so the regression landed on main uncaught and only PR CI surfaced it.
- Exact fix commit not bisected (24 commits in `8a92dacf4..e8ae7a29`); not
  decision-relevant since the rebase target is current main HEAD regardless. Can bisect
  on request.

## Remediation (DECISION NEEDED — bulk + outward-facing)
**Rebase the 11 CI-failing PRs onto current `main` (e8ae7a29 or later) and push.**
A bare CI "re-run" reuses the old merge SHA and will NOT pick up the main fix — the
branch must be rebased/merged so CI re-tests against fixed main.

11 PRs to rebase (all authored by quad341 / ours):
- #3919, #4160, #3971, #4163, #3663, #3914, #3710, #4153, #3908, #3906, #4055

**Done-when (per PR):** `PR Risk` → `Test (Embedded Dolt Cmd 8/20 & 12/20)` green;
`CI Gate / Required` green.

This is mechanical and a good fit for `beads/builder`, but it is **11 force-pushes to
upstream PRs** (re-triggers upstream CI en masse) — hence routed to mayor for go/no-go
before slinging to builder. Mayor: reply / sling to `beads/builder` to execute.

## Separate: 5 "stale audit" PRs (NOT this root cause)
#3987, #4228, #4023, #3913, #3632 — **0 failing checks**, just old (last touched
May 19–Jun 6). These need a keep / rebase / close / supersede triage decision
(maintainer/mayor call). Per memory `beads-pr-ours-mergeable-is-terminal`, if any are
ours + green + mergeable they are terminal (awaiting upstream maintainer merge, no
contributor action). Audit beads for these left OPEN pending triage.

## Process notes (for mayor)
1. **Double-filing:** the 16 audit items were each filed twice — an `order:pr-audit`
   leaf bead AND a `deacon` "Pick up bead be-XXXX" sling wrapper = 32 beads for 16 PRs.
   Worth de-duping the audit→sling pipeline.
2. **CI-coverage gap:** `PR Risk` (embedded `-race` routed tests) does not run on main
   push, so this regression merged to main uncaught. Consider gating main-push CI on the
   embedded `-race` shard (note `6a1e7af9b` already added lines to `main.yml`).

Durable note saved: `bd remember` key `beads-pr-risk-routed-readonly-regression-jun11`.
Investigated by beads/investigator, 2026-06-13.
notes:
UPDATE (same session): the 5 stale-audit PRs (#3987 #4228 #4023 #3913 #3632) are now RESOLVED, not pending. All are ours+OPEN+MERGEABLE+CI-green (22-51 checks, 0 fail/0 pending) with no review threads, so closed as TERMINAL — awaiting upstream maintainer merge, no contributor action — per standing ruling gm-wisp-4po3eg. Their 10 beads (5 leaf + 5 wrapper) are CLOSED. The ONLY open decision for mayor is item 1: rebase the 11 CI-failing PRs (mechanical, 11 upstream force-pushes, your go/no-go → sling builder). Process items (a) double-filing and (b) main-push CI coverage still stand. Investigator routed queue now empty.

title: Daily standup — 2026-06-13
description:
# Daily standup — plain-English status for mayor

You are the rig PM. Mayor reads this in the morning. Write the brief and close this bead.

## Format (use this exact shape)

### What was done (last ~24h)
Concrete bullets. Recent closures, merges, decisions, fixes. Bead IDs go in parens for anchoring, NOT as primary content. Terse bullets, not paragraphs.

### What's in flight
Active arcs, who's working what. Group by theme if multiple. Plain English — a colleague who's been out a day should understand.

### What's blocking
Anything stuck. Why. What needs to move (a decision, a bead, an upstream landing). If nothing is blocking, write "nothing".

### What's next
The things that should land in the next ~24h if all goes well.

### Questions for mayor (optional — omit if none)
ONLY include if you actually need operator input. Don't ask permission for things you can decide yourself. Examples of valid asks:
- A scope/priority/sequencing decision only mayor can make
- A blocker needing operator action (lift a freeze, choose an option from a real set)
- Confirmation when you're about to do something potentially destructive or wide-blast

NOT valid asks (these are PM's call, just decide):
- "Should we revisit retired feature X?" — your call; default is stay-shelved unless evidence forces a revisit
- Internal-system architecture/sequencing decisions that need deep context — your call
- Routine rescheduling, deferring, dropping work — you're empowered

If this section is non-empty, mail mayor after closing the bead:
`gc mail send mayor -s "Re: standup $(date +%Y-%m-%d)" -m "Questions in <bead-id> — please advise"`

## Style

- **Plain English, not bead-ID dumps.** Lead with what's happening; cite beads in parens for anchoring.
- Concrete > abstract. Names of files / commits / branches where relevant.
- You are empowered to revisit, reschedule, drop, or escalate things without permission. Mayor appreciates autonomy. Surface questions only when mayor's perspective genuinely matters.
- Be honest about red flags — if something looks wrong, say so plainly.

## Deliverable

Write the standup into this bead's `notes` (use `bd update <this-bead-id> --notes "..."`).
Then close the bead with a one-line reason like "standup posted".

If you raised mayor-questions in section 5, also send the mail described above.

Current main HEAD e8ae7a291a (feat(count): add --include-infra, PR #4389) — 30/30 CI checks passing. Root causes A/B/C from be-119p are healed upstream. Main was red ~3 days; the blocker has lifted.

**Implication:** Every PR previously closed as inherited-terminal will need a fresh CI run via rebase. Hourly pr-audit should resurface them. **be-xw20 (PR #3813):** Decision bead still open; awaiting mayor confirmation to close/withdraw.

Nothing structural. Main green removes the primary blocker. New constraint: each stranded PR now needs an actual rebase + CI re-run; investigator will process as pr-audit cycle routes them.

## What's next

- Investigator re-triages all open CI-failing pr-audit beads now that main is green.

2. **be-119p**: Main is now green. The B fix (PR #4367) was NOT what fixed it — upstream healed via a separate path. Can we close be-119p as 'resolved upstream'? (Or should we leave open in case it re-reddens?)

# Daily standup — plain-English status for mayor

You are the rig PM. Mayor reads this in the morning. Write the brief and close this bead.

## Format (use this exact shape)

### What was done (last ~24h)
Concrete bullets. Recent closures, merges, decisions, fixes. Bead IDs go in parens for anchoring, NOT as primary content. Terse bullets, not paragraphs.

### What's in flight
Active arcs, who's working what. Group by theme if multiple. Plain English — a colleague who's been out a day should understand.

### What's blocking
Anything stuck. Why. What needs to move (a decision, a bead, an upstream landing). If nothing is blocking, write "nothing".

### What's next
The things that should land in the next ~24h if all goes well.

### Questions for mayor (optional — omit if none)
ONLY include if you actually need operator input. Don't ask permission for things you can decide yourself. Examples of valid asks:
- A scope/priority/sequencing decision only mayor can make
- A blocker needing operator action (lift a freeze, choose an option from a real set)
- Confirmation when you're about to do something potentially destructive or wide-blast

NOT valid asks (these are PM's call, just decide):
- "Should we revisit retired feature X?" — your call; default is stay-shelved unless evidence forces a revisit
- Internal-system architecture/sequencing decisions that need deep context — your call
- Routine rescheduling, deferring, dropping work — you're empowered

If this section is non-empty, mail mayor after closing the bead:
`gc mail send mayor -s "Re: standup $(date +%Y-%m-%d)" -m "Questions in <bead-id> — please advise"`

## Style

- **Plain English, not bead-ID dumps.** Lead with what's happening; cite beads in parens for anchoring.
- Concrete > abstract. Names of files / commits / branches where relevant.
- You are empowered to revisit, reschedule, drop, or escalate things without permission. Mayor appreciates autonomy. Surface questions only when mayor's perspective genuinely matters.
- Be honest about red flags — if something looks wrong, say so plainly.

## Deliverable

Write the standup into this bead's `notes` (use `bd update <this-bead-id> --notes "..."`).
Then close the bead with a one-line reason like "standup posted".

If you raised mayor-questions in section 5, also send the mail described above.

title: Upstream main RED (gastownhall/beads): bd-6dnrw.29-34 batch — errcheck + embeddeddolt read-only regression
description:
## Summary
gastownhall/beads `main` is RED on the "Main" workflow and has been since the
bd-6dnrw.29-34 batch (Steve Yegge, upstream maintainer) landed 2026-06-10 ~03:00Z.
Last GREEN main: 99c70904f (2026-06-10T02:53Z). First RED: f1c72dbde (03:22Z).
This blocks EVERY open PR, including 3 "CI failing" pr-audit beads routed to
investigator (#3710/be-uqdb, #3919/be-ef0u, #4153/be-2ajx). Those PRs are NOT
individually broken — they inherit a broken main. No per-PR fix helps until
main is green.

All culprit commits are UPSTREAM maintainer work (bd-6dnrw series). We are
contributors, not maintainers. Per gm-qggepi / beads-pr-ours-mergeable-is-terminal,
investigator does not unilaterally fix or comment on upstream main. Escalating
to mayor for the decision on how/whether to surface upstream or fast-track a
contributor fix PR.

## Proven root causes (2 primary)

### A. Lint / Build Artifacts (errcheck)  — culprit f483ac2b4 (bd-6dnrw.31)
- Site: cmd/bd/bootstrap.go:694  `fmt.Fprint(w, ...)` return value unchecked.
- Why now: CI installs golangci-lint via `latest` -> resolved v2.12.2, which no
  longer honors the `fmt.Fprint` entry in .golangci.yml errcheck.exclude-functions
  (the entry IS present, lines 33 & 36). The lint cache masks the identical
  pattern in 10 OTHER untouched files (federation.go:365, main.go:1042/1091/1102,
  list_output.go:21, list_input.go:146, ado_test.go x4). f483ac2b4 modified
  bootstrap.go -> cache miss -> fresh analysis flagged it. The other 10 will
  fail the moment their files are next touched.
- Fix (immediate, unblocks lint): change line 694 to `_, _ = fmt.Fprint(w, ...)`
  (matches the cmd/bd/ado.go convention).
- Fix (root): pin golangci-lint off `latest` to a known-good version, AND/OR
  repair errcheck.exclude-functions for golangci-lint v2 semantics so the
  fmt.Fprint exclude is honored again.

### B. Embedded Dolt Cmd tests (read-only regression) — culprit 3f2b4e08d (bd-6dnrw.32)
- Failing test: cmd/bd/update_embedded_test.go:190
  TestEmbeddedUpdateRoutedStoreCommitsTargetHead
  -> "Error updating tgt-4ha: embeddeddolt: store is read-only" (exit 1).
  Also fails shards Cmd 8/20, 12/20, 14/20 and Embedded Dolt Storage on main.
- Culprit 3f2b4e08d "fix(embeddeddolt): give read-only opens a real read-only
  path": introduced errReadOnly + a `readOnly bool` field + OpenReadOnly(), and
  changed cmd/bd/store_factory.go (the routing layer). The routed-update WRITE
  path now selects a read-only open and refuses the write.
- Fix: ensure the routed / target-head update path opens a WRITABLE store.
  OpenReadOnly must be reserved for cross-repo hydration of foreign projects
  (GH#3231), not the routed-write path. Likely a store_factory.go routing
  condition regression.

## Secondary / unconfirmed
- "Check doc flags freshness" and "PR Policy (wrapper timing)" also fail on the
  same main runs, but their --log-failed output was dominated by checkout/cleanup
  and did not surface a precise reason. Likely cascading from A/B or separate;
  needs a maintainer / deeper log pull.

## Evidence
- main "Main" runs: 1fe4993cf, dc0561af2, f1c72dbde all FAILURE; last green 99c70904f.
- Ancestry: a0f9b880e (#4141) EXONERATED (in green main); the 6 window commits are
  bd-6dnrw.29-34 (f1c72dbde, 8ffcf698e, ccadfce9f, 3f2b4e08d, f483ac2b4, 0664ee7be).
- bootstrap.go:694 blame = f483ac2b4; 10 sibling bare fmt.Fprint calls unflagged.
- 3f2b4e08d adds errReadOnly + OpenReadOnly + touches store_factory.go.

## Disposition of the 7 routed pr-audit beads
- CI-failing (inherit broken main, no per-PR defect): be-uqdb #3710, be-ef0u #3919
  (also CONFLICTING - needs rebase, but rebase won't green it while main is red),
  be-2ajx #4153 -> closed, pointing here.
- Green/mergeable (ours, awaiting upstream maintainer merge per standing ruling;
  stale-green - last CI ran against the older green main): be-80qp #3906,
  be-lpyz #3908, be-xz6v #4160, be-7l5n #4213 -> closed per policy.

Latest main (88d1c2b5e, run 27360198790 @16:02Z) is STILL RED. Root cause B

remains unfixed upstream. Confirmed the IDENTICAL failure on PR #3914 (Embedded Dolt

title: Daily standup — 2026-06-11
description:
# Daily standup — plain-English status for mayor

You are the rig PM. Mayor reads this in the morning. Write the brief and close this bead.

## Format (use this exact shape)

### What was done (last ~24h)
Concrete bullets. Recent closures, merges, decisions, fixes. Bead IDs go in parens for anchoring, NOT as primary content. Terse bullets, not paragraphs.

### What's in flight
Active arcs, who's working what. Group by theme if multiple. Plain English — a colleague who's been out a day should understand.

### What's blocking
Anything stuck. Why. What needs to move (a decision, a bead, an upstream landing). If nothing is blocking, write "nothing".

### What's next
The things that should land in the next ~24h if all goes well.

### Questions for mayor (optional — omit if none)
ONLY include if you actually need operator input. Don't ask permission for things you can decide yourself. Examples of valid asks:
- A scope/priority/sequencing decision only mayor can make
- A blocker needing operator action (lift a freeze, choose an option from a real set)
- Confirmation when you're about to do something potentially destructive or wide-blast

NOT valid asks (these are PM's call, just decide):
- "Should we revisit retired feature X?" — your call; default is stay-shelved unless evidence forces a revisit
- Internal-system architecture/sequencing decisions that need deep context — your call
- Routine rescheduling, deferring, dropping work — you're empowered

If this section is non-empty, mail mayor after closing the bead:
`gc mail send mayor -s "Re: standup $(date +%Y-%m-%d)" -m "Questions in <bead-id> — please advise"`

## Style

- **Plain English, not bead-ID dumps.** Lead with what's happening; cite beads in parens for anchoring.
- Concrete > abstract. Names of files / commits / branches where relevant.
- You are empowered to revisit, reschedule, drop, or escalate things without permission. Mayor appreciates autonomy. Surface questions only when mayor's perspective genuinely matters.
- Be honest about red flags — if something looks wrong, say so plainly.

## Deliverable

Write the standup into this bead's `notes` (use `bd update <this-bead-id> --notes "..."`).
Then close the bead with a one-line reason like "standup posted".

If you raised mayor-questions in section 5, also send the mail described above.
notes:

- **Routed-write main RED resolved** — beads main was RED ~18h on a `store is read-only` regression in embeddeddolt routed writes (regressor 3f2b4e08d, bd-6dnrw.32). Full investigation and fix completed: architecture decision made (be-4hzi), two implementation layers built and reviewed (be-w9fg: OpenWritable + RoutedSchemaBehindError + checkBackwardDrift; be-jb55: newWritableNoMigrateStoreFromConfig + routing factory rename), deployed gate ran, PR #4367 opened. All CI fully green, mergeable — awaiting upstream maintainer merge.
- **PR #4158 audit closed** (be-bocy) — terminal-ready, ours, all CI green; awaiting upstream maintainer merge. No contributor action.
- **PR #3458 audit closed** (be-muoe) — dealt with.
- **MPR stranded-PR fix** in gc-management — clear-hold now properly completes the blessed merge without stranding open PRs (gm-0yv9h).

### What's in flight

- **PR #4367** (fix/routed-write-readonly-regression) — fully CI green, MERGEABLE, open; awaiting gastownhall maintainer merge.
- **PR audit queue** — seven CI-failing or stale audits queued as ready beads: #3710 (37d, be-uqdb), #3906 (30d, be-80qp), #3908 (30d, be-lpyz), #3919 (29d, be-ef0u), #4153 (be-2ajx), #4160 (16d, be-xz6v), #4213 (14d, be-7l5n).

title: Fix: renumber PR #3663 migration 0050->0051 (dup-version collision with main #4259)
description:
## Root cause

PR #3663 (`fix(dolt): PURGE dropped databases after DROP`, branch
`quad341/release/be-1n9-pq5-purge`, OURS) adds migration
`internal/storage/schema/migrations/0050_add_date_indexes.{up,down}.sql`.

Since the PR's last green CI (2026-06-03), `origin/main` landed a DIFFERENT
migration `0050_dependencies_deterministic_id` via PR #4259 (2026-06-07). Both
filenames parse to schema version **50** (numeric prefix parse at
`internal/storage/schema/schema.go:189`).

The embedded-migration loader has an explicit duplicate-version guard at
`internal/storage/schema/schema.go:619-625` that **panics** on a duplicate
version, and CI's "Check no duplicate migration versions" step
(`.github/workflows/pr.yml:131-144`) fails the build before any Go build.

GitHub reports PR #3663 as `MERGEABLE` / `CLEAN` ONLY because git sees two
differently-named new files (no textual conflict). It does not understand
migration-version semantics. The PR's green status rollup is therefore STALE
(pre-#4259); a fresh CI run against current main fails the duplicate-version
check, and merging would land two version-50 migrations and panic the schema
loader on every startup.

`origin/main`'s current max migration version is 0050, so **0051 is free**.

## Reproducing test / proof

- `git ls-tree origin/main internal/storage/schema/migrations/ | grep 0050`
  shows `0050_dependencies_deterministic_id.{up,down}.sql` on main.
- PR head still carries `0050_add_date_indexes.{up,down}.sql` (verified via
  `gh pr view 3663 --json files`).
- Merging the two => two version-50 migrations => panic at schema.go:619
  ("schema: duplicate migration version 50 ... renumber one before commit")
  and CI "Check no duplicate migration versions" => FAIL.

## Fix spec (renumber 0050 -> 0051; SQL content unchanged)

Work in the beads rig (`/home/jaword/projects/beads`). Remotes there:
`fork` = quad341 (PR head lives here), `origin` = gastownhall. Honor
`TMPDIR=$HOME/.gotmp GOTMPDIR=$HOME/.gotmp` for Go builds (/tmp quota).

1. Checkout the PR branch:
   `git fetch fork && git checkout release/be-1n9-pq5-purge && git pull --ff-only fork release/be-1n9-pq5-purge`
   (Renumbering on the branch is sufficient to clear the collision — no rebase

description:
## Decision needed
Withdraw (close) PR #3813 on gastownhall/beads, or keep it open?

**Recommendation: WITHDRAW / CLOSE as not-applicable-to-upstream.**

## PR
- https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/3813 — "fix(utils): be-szr ResolvePartialID falls through to GetIssue for wisps (PG)"
- Head: quad341/beads-sec003-contrib @ fix/be-szr-pg-wisp-resolve -> base gastownhall/beads:main (cross-repo; ours, author quad341)
- Open 33d; mergeable=MERGEABLE / mergeStateStatus=CLEAN / all CI green; reviewDecision = NONE.

## Outstanding maintainer ask (UNADDRESSED)
coffeegoddd (upstream maintainer), 2026-05-10 [COMMENTED review]:
> "We need a beads-only minimal repro of the bug, otherwise this is a bug with your orchestration layer."
Our later replies were a code-reading verification (2026-05-08) + an internal beads/reviewer PASS (2026-05-19). Neither provides the requested repro.

## Investigation finding (evidence)
The 1-file diff adds a `store.GetIssue(ctx, input)` fallback in ResolvePartialID (internal/utils/id_parser.go, immediately after the SearchIssues exact-ID fast path). Its sole justification is PG-backend behavior: on Postgres, SearchIssues does not merge ephemeral wisps, but GetIssue falls through issues->wisps.

- Upstream gastownhall/beads main has NO postgres backend. internal/storage is Dolt-only (dolt, embeddeddolt + support pkgs). [authoritative: gh api repos/gastownhall/beads/contents/internal/storage?ref=main]
- The PR's own fork branch tree is ALSO Dolt-only: internal/storage/postgres 404s on quad341/beads-sec003-contrib@fix/be-szr-pg-wisp-resolve.
- On the supported Dolt backend, full wisp IDs ALREADY resolve via the SearchIssues wisp-merge (internal/storage/issueops/search.go:48; internal/storage/dolt/iter_issues.go:9). Proven by the PRE-EXISTING on-main test internal/utils/id_parser_test.go:870 `TestResolvePartialID_Wisp`, which includes the "full wisp ID" case. The PR does not add/modify that test (changedFiles=1, id_parser.go only) and it is green in the PR's own Embedded-Dolt CI matrix. => the GetIssue fallback is a NO-OP / dead code on Dolt.

=> coffeegoddd was correct: the bug only manifests on our PG infra (the "orchestration layer"), which is not part of upstream beads. A beads-only minimal repro on a supported backend is IMPOSSIBLE.

(Could not run the Dolt test live in the investigator worktree: Docker daemon is down here and the test needs the shared Dolt container. Evidence is structural via the GitHub API + the test's presence and greenness in upstream CI.)

## Options
- (A, RECOMMENDED) Withdraw/close PR #3813, optionally with a one-line courtesy reply to coffeegoddd thanking them and confirming it is PG-infra-specific (our fork), not an upstream beads bug. Clears the maintainer's queue; stops recurring stale-audits.
- (B) Leave open indefinitely: mild clutter on the maintainer's queue; will keep generating monthly stale-audit beads.
- (C) Re-scope: nothing to re-scope; there is no Dolt-observable bug.

## Related (also moot upstream if PG is not an upstream backend)
- be-szr (originating bug bead) was closed "superseded by this PR"; if withdrawn, its PG fix never lands, but be-szr is itself PG-only -> moot on Dolt-only upstream.
- be-ekw (gated follow-up: partial wisp IDs on PG) is likewise PG-only -> moot upstream.

## Why routed to mayor, not executed by investigator
Closing a PR on the upstream repo is an outward, public action where the maintainer is engaged, and PG-backend dispositions are gated to mayor greenlight (project memory project_pg_backend_followups_gated). I did not close or comment on the PR.

## Format (use this exact shape)

Concrete bullets. Recent closures, merges, decisions, fixes. Bead IDs go in parens for anchoring, NOT as primary content. Terse bullets, not paragraphs.

### What's in flight
Active arcs, who's working what. Group by theme if multiple. Plain English — a colleague who's been out a day should understand.

### What's blocking
Anything stuck. Why. What needs to move (a decision, a bead, an upstream landing). If nothing is blocking, write "nothing".

### What's next
The things that should land in the next ~24h if all goes well.

### Questions for mayor (optional — omit if none)
ONLY include if you actually need operator input. Don't ask permission for things you can decide yourself. Examples of valid asks:
- A scope/priority/sequencing decision only mayor can make

title: Daily standup — 2026-06-06
description:
# Daily standup — plain-English status for mayor

You are the rig PM. Mayor reads this in the morning. Write the brief and close this bead.

## Format (use this exact shape)

### What was done (last ~24h)
Concrete bullets. Recent closures, merges, decisions, fixes. Bead IDs go in parens for anchoring, NOT as primary content. Terse bullets, not paragraphs.

### What's in flight
Active arcs, who's working what. Group by theme if multiple. Plain English — a colleague who's been out a day should understand.

### What's blocking
Anything stuck. Why. What needs to move (a decision, a bead, an upstream landing). If nothing is blocking, write "nothing".

### What's next
The things that should land in the next ~24h if all goes well.

### Questions for mayor (optional — omit if none)
ONLY include if you actually need operator input. Don't ask permission for things you can decide yourself. Examples of valid asks:
- A scope/priority/sequencing decision only mayor can make
- A blocker needing operator action (lift a freeze, choose an option from a real set)
- Confirmation when you're about to do something potentially destructive or wide-blast

NOT valid asks (these are PM's call, just decide):
- "Should we revisit retired feature X?" — your call; default is stay-shelved unless evidence forces a revisit
- Internal-system architecture/sequencing decisions that need deep context — your call
- Routine rescheduling, deferring, dropping work — you're empowered

If this section is non-empty, mail mayor after closing the bead:
`gc mail send mayor -s "Re: standup $(date +%Y-%m-%d)" -m "Questions in <bead-id> — please advise"`

## Style

- **Plain English, not bead-ID dumps.** Lead with what's happening; cite beads in parens for anchoring.
- Concrete > abstract. Names of files / commits / branches where relevant.
- You are empowered to revisit, reschedule, drop, or escalate things without permission. Mayor appreciates autonomy. Surface questions only when mayor's perspective genuinely matters.
- Be honest about red flags — if something looks wrong, say so plainly.

## Deliverable

Write the standup into this bead's `notes` (use `bd update <this-bead-id> --notes "..."`).
Then close the bead with a one-line reason like "standup posted".

If you raised mayor-questions in section 5, also send the mail described above.
notes:
## What was done (last ~24h)

- Mayor delivered settled policy (gm-wisp-de1ldw): beads PRs (gastownhall/beads) are upstream — we do NOT merge, NOT authorize GC_MPR_ALLOW_UNMAINTAINED=1. These are 'authored, awaiting upstream.' Per-session CLEAN checks stop now.
- PR #4028 (fork-detect contributor routing, be-wqt8) confirmed merged to main earlier.
- Recent commits landed on origin/main: docgen CGO-binary federation guard (be-3cse, f288253ad), planning-schema fork fix (#4290, 0da7f51f3).
- Stale PR audits processed by reviewer: be-lehc (PR #3662), be-l13z (PR #3618), be-z6qf (PR #3998) — all closed.

## What's in flight

- **bd-lfak Phase 3** (bd preflight --fix): all implementation + test beads closed. PRs #4022, #4053, #4054, #4055 authored and CLEAN/MERGEABLE. Policy now: track as 'authored, awaiting upstream' — no more per-session status checks.
- be-fe4y (submit test PR) remains open, blocked on #4054 upstream merge. Same status.
- Sentry/mol-witness wisps cycling normally.

## What's blocking

- PRs #4022/#4053/#4054/#4055: gastownhall/beads maintainers must merge. Per today's policy this is not a GC action item — we wait.
- be-fe4y: blocked on #4054 upstream merge (same).

## What's next

- Update bd-lfak plan to drop per-session CLEAN check language; mark 'authored, awaiting upstream.'
- Check for any new work (architect/designer handoffs).

## Questions for mayor (optional)

None — today's policy message settles the open questions.

Verdict: PREMISE OBSOLETE -- recommend CLOSE (no-longer-wanted) or REWORK. Exit (d): escalated to mayor (close/rework is a maintainer/product call, not this seat).

Verified vs fresh origin/main:
- Ours (author quad341). MERGEABLE, ALL CI green, purely additive (+144/-0: cmd/bd/main.go guard + cmd/bd/main_errors_test.go + release gate). No inline/review comments; only codecov bot (80% patch coverage -- not a blocker).
- PR adds checkMetadataBackendError(): if metadata.json declares backend != dolt (e.g. postgres), FatalError "This bd binary does not support the <backend> backend... Upgrade bd to a version that supports <backend>: curl install.sh | bash; brew upgrade beads".

Why the premise drifted:
- Postgres was a real backend effort (feat(postgres): bd init --backend=postgres, --pg-* flags, PG health/bench) that was SCRUBBED from the public codebase: be-bhrzia "scrub pgx/postgres from public beads codebase", committed 2026-05-16 22:21 UTC -- ~2.5h AFTER this PR was filed (2026-05-16 19:49 UTC). Same-day concurrent work; the PR landed on the wrong side of the scrub.
- Current public origin/main: NO postgres. init_postgres*/postgres_health.go gone, no pgx, `bd init` only supports --backend dolt. configfile.Backend is "Deprecated: always dolt"; GetBackend() unconditionally returns dolt; startup path does NOT read the raw .Backend field for behavior (PR's guard reads it; nothing else does).

Consequences on current main:
1) Guard remediation is UNFOLLOWABLE: it tells users to upgrade via public install.sh/brew to "a version that supports postgres", but the public binary is dolt-only -- no such public version exists. Misleading advice shipped to users.
2) The motivating symptom (stale pre-PG binary silently entering multi-GB/30-60s postgres fallback, be-y0sm9s/be-bx0tm7) likely NO LONGER reproduces: no postgres code path remains; backend=postgres is simply ignored (treated as dolt via GetBackend()).

Out-of-rig open question for mayor: there is a `no_dolt` build tag for a "PG-only bd binary" (be-mlavwq) -- postgres may survive behind a build tag / private repo. Even so, the PUBLIC channels the error names don't restore postgres, so the message is wrong for the public binary regardless. (Did not chase private-PG topology; not needed to decide this public PR.)

Recommendation to mayor: CLOSE PR #3998 as no-longer-wanted (premise obsolete). If a generic "unsupported/unknown backend -> clear error" guard is still wanted, REWORK the message into a removal/migration hint (not "upgrade for postgres support") -- an architecture/product call. Did NOT post on GitHub (city policy). Escalated via mail.

### What was done (last ~24h)
Concrete bullets. Recent closures, merges, decisions, fixes. Bead IDs go in parens for anchoring, NOT as primary content. Terse bullets, not paragraphs.

### What's in flight
Active arcs, who's working what. Group by theme if multiple. Plain English — a colleague who's been out a day should understand.

### What's blocking
Anything stuck. Why. What needs to move (a decision, a bead, an upstream landing). If nothing is blocking, write "nothing".

### What's next
The things that should land in the next ~24h if all goes well.

### Questions for mayor (optional — omit if none)
ONLY include if you actually need operator input. Don't ask permission for things you can decide yourself. Examples of valid asks:
- A scope/priority/sequencing decision only mayor can make

title: Harden generate-cli-docs.sh against CGO-binary federation doc drift
description:
## Root cause
generate-cli-docs.sh selects its bd binary as: $1, else $PROJECT_ROOT/bd, else builds CGO_ENABLED=0 -tags gms_pure_go. When a CGO-enabled ./bd is left in PROJECT_ROOT (e.g. from `make build` during a builder/deployer session), a no-arg call regenerates docs from it. A CGO bd exposes the CGO-only `bd federation` subcommands, so the regen writes federation subcommand pages into docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md, website/{docs,versioned_docs/version-*}/cli-reference/federation.md and website/static/llms-full.txt. CI's check-doc-flags builds CGO_ENABLED=0 (scripts/ci/pr-policy.sh build_docs_binary) whose bd emits NO federation subcommands -> doc-flags fails and cascades to Build Artifacts / PR Policy / CI Gate. Hit PRs #3710, #4055, #4153 simultaneously on 2026-06-06 (each fixed by regenerating with a pure-go binary).

## Fix spec
In scripts/generate-cli-docs.sh, make doc generation CI-consistent regardless of stray binaries. Recommended: after resolving $BD, probe it (`"$BD" federation --help`) and if it does NOT print the "Federation commands require CGO" stub (i.e. it is a CGO build that exposes subcommands), either (a) ignore it and build a fresh CGO_ENABLED=0 binary internally, or (b) abort with a clear message instructing to pass a CGO_ENABLED=0 build. Prefer (a) for robustness; keep the explicit-arg fast path only when the arg is already pure-go. Apply the same guard to the $PROJECT_ROOT/bd fallback. Add a one-line comment pointing at scripts/ci/pr-policy.sh build_docs_binary as the oracle.

## Out of scope
- Do NOT remove the CGO-only federation subcommands or change CGO build behavior.
- Do NOT touch check-doc-flags.sh / check-doc-freshness.sh / pr-policy.sh.
- Do NOT regenerate committed docs in this bead (that is per-PR work).

## Done-when
- [ ] Running generate-cli-docs.sh with a CGO ./bd present in PROJECT_ROOT no longer emits federation subcommand pages (matches CGO_ENABLED=0 output).
- [ ] LC_ALL=C ./scripts/generate-cli-docs.sh <pure-go bd> still produces zero churn on a clean main.
- [ ] check-doc-flags.sh + check-doc-freshness.sh pass after a regen on main.
- [ ] A short note in the script references the CGO_ENABLED=0 CI oracle.
close_reason: Implemented CGO guard in generate-cli-docs.sh. After resolving bd binary, probes 'bd federation --help'; if no pure-go stub, rebuilds CGO_ENABLED=0 binary internally. All done-when criteria met. PR #4312 (quad341:fix/be-3cse-cgo-docgen-guard → gastownhall/beads main).

# Daily standup — plain-English status for mayor

You are the rig PM. Mayor reads this in the morning. Write the brief and close this bead.

## Format (use this exact shape)

### What was done (last ~24h)
Concrete bullets. Recent closures, merges, decisions, fixes. Bead IDs go in parens for anchoring, NOT as primary content. Terse bullets, not paragraphs.

### What's in flight
Active arcs, who's working what. Group by theme if multiple. Plain English — a colleague who's been out a day should understand.

### What's blocking
Anything stuck. Why. What needs to move (a decision, a bead, an upstream landing). If nothing is blocking, write "nothing".

### What's next
The things that should land in the next ~24h if all goes well.

### Questions for mayor (optional — omit if none)
ONLY include if you actually need operator input. Don't ask permission for things you can decide yourself. Examples of valid asks:
- A scope/priority/sequencing decision only mayor can make
- A blocker needing operator action (lift a freeze, choose an option from a real set)
- Confirmation when you're about to do something potentially destructive or wide-blast

NOT valid asks (these are PM's call, just decide):
- "Should we revisit retired feature X?" — your call; default is stay-shelved unless evidence forces a revisit
- Internal-system architecture/sequencing decisions that need deep context — your call
- Routine rescheduling, deferring, dropping work — you're empowered

If this section is non-empty, mail mayor after closing the bead:
`gc mail send mayor -s "Re: standup $(date +%Y-%m-%d)" -m "Questions in <bead-id> — please advise"`

- **Plain English, not bead-ID dumps.** Lead with what's happening; cite beads in parens for anchoring.
- Concrete > abstract. Names of files / commits / branches where relevant.
- You are empowered to revisit, reschedule, drop, or escalate things without permission. Mayor appreciates autonomy. Surface questions only when mayor's perspective genuinely matters.
- Be honest about red flags — if something looks wrong, say so plainly.

Write the standup into this bead's `notes` (use `bd update <this-bead-id> --notes "..."`).

title: Daily standup — 2026-06-03
description:
# Daily standup — plain-English status for mayor

You are the rig PM. Mayor reads this in the morning. Write the brief and close this bead.

## Format (use this exact shape)

### What was done (last ~24h)
Concrete bullets. Recent closures, merges, decisions, fixes. Bead IDs go in parens for anchoring, NOT as primary content. Terse bullets, not paragraphs.

### What's in flight
Active arcs, who's working what. Group by theme if multiple. Plain English — a colleague who's been out a day should understand.

### What's blocking
Anything stuck. Why. What needs to move (a decision, a bead, an upstream landing). If nothing is blocking, write "nothing".

### What's next
The things that should land in the next ~24h if all goes well.

### Questions for mayor (optional — omit if none)
ONLY include if you actually need operator input. Don't ask permission for things you can decide yourself. Examples of valid asks:
- A scope/priority/sequencing decision only mayor can make
- A blocker needing operator action (lift a freeze, choose an option from a real set)
- Confirmation when you're about to do something potentially destructive or wide-blast

NOT valid asks (these are PM's call, just decide):
- "Should we revisit retired feature X?" — your call; default is stay-shelved unless evidence forces a revisit
- Internal-system architecture/sequencing decisions that need deep context — your call
- Routine rescheduling, deferring, dropping work — you're empowered

If this section is non-empty, mail mayor after closing the bead:
`gc mail send mayor -s "Re: standup $(date +%Y-%m-%d)" -m "Questions in <bead-id> — please advise"`

## Style

- **Plain English, not bead-ID dumps.** Lead with what's happening; cite beads in parens for anchoring.
- Concrete > abstract. Names of files / commits / branches where relevant.
- You are empowered to revisit, reschedule, drop, or escalate things without permission. Mayor appreciates autonomy. Surface questions only when mayor's perspective genuinely matters.
- Be honest about red flags — if something looks wrong, say so plainly.

## Deliverable

Write the standup into this bead's `notes` (use `bd update <this-bead-id> --notes "..."`).
Then close the bead with a one-line reason like "standup posted".

If you raised mayor-questions in section 5, also send the mail described above.
notes:
### What was done (last ~24h)

- **PR #4023 (reference-aware bd prune) fixed and green.** Investigator diagnosed the root cause (main's wholesale doc regen on 2026-06-03 dropped the newly-added `migrate-personal.md` page from the 1.0.5 versioned snapshot, killing doc-flags CI). Fix: regenerated via `generate-cli-docs.sh ./bd`, committed, pushed. All 51 CI checks now pass — PR is PASS (maphew review) + green; merge-ready (be-nzyb).
- **PR #4058 (--quiet flag wiring) escalated to mayor.** Investigator confirmed: still novel vs main, already approved in pack review, only step left is merge authority. Mayor has mail (be-g438).
- **PR #4059 (bd doctor --check=pollution docs) escalated to mayor.** Same situation — docs-only, CI green, pack-approved, no code fix needed. Mayor has mail (be-68h0).
- **PR #4300 merged** (proxied server list command, coffeegoddd). PR #4299 also merged (community tools website page).
- **Narrow-projection perf arc active on branch**: `SearchIssueSummaries` added (be-3ht), release gate PASS committed, `WispIDSetInTx` amortization landed, unit tests for `sortSummaries`/`useSummary` in (be-2kl). Rebased onto main's `WispIDSetInTx(ids)` API (be-el0). Not yet in a PR.

### What's in flight

- **Schema-skew detection family (be-4259)**: PRs #4266 (deterministic dep PKs), #4268 (silent-migration prevention gate), #4269 (parallel t.Setenv fix), #4270 (per-migration content hash + bd doctor skew detection) — all open, awaiting review/merge.
- **GitLab dependency sync** (#4294) — open, awaiting review.
- **Conflicting-deps fix** (#4286, six typed dep tables) — open, has one comment but no blocking review.
- **Other infra fixes in queue**: #4288 (skip empty dolt commit), #4284 (bound embedded dolt timeout), #4281 (dolt push hooks), #4290 (planning init fork fix), #4296 (dolt federation runtime dir discriminator), #4289 (index metadata fields).
- **Witness-patrol mol** (be-wpuv) cycling — substeps open for orphan reset, queue depth report, and next patrol iteration.

### What's blocking

- PRs #4023, #4058, #4059 are all merge-ready but need merge authority (operator/mayor/mpr). Investigator escalated #4058 and #4059 to mayor via mail; #4023 is also waiting.
- No code defects blocking any of the above — pure pipeline throughput.

### What's next

- Mayor action on #4058 and #4059 (two ours-authored PRs, both approved, safe to merge).
- Merge #4023 (reference-aware prune, green + PASS review).
- Review pass on #4286 (conflicting deps) — it has a comment that may need a response before it clears.
